title: The Nicene faith is catholic and apostolic, and sufficient on the Spirit
english: We recognize the holy synod of the fathers at Nicaea as truly catholic and apostolic, and we guard the faith set forth by the fathers at that time, praying that it may remain unmoved and unshaken forever. It became necessary then for the fathers to explain more fully the glory of the Only Begotten, because they were eager to cut off the recently sprouting heresy of Arius, cutting away its first seeds beforehand, before the thorn became fully hardened. But since the question concerning the Spirit was then still silenced, they added nothing more extensive about it. Yet for those who read intelligently, the teaching about the Spirit in that creed is sufficient. Just as they decreed belief in the Father and the Son, so also they decreed belief in the Spirit, neither introducing any other nature into the divine and blessed Trinity nor cutting off any member of the Trinity from the statement of faith. But since Satan, attempting afresh to shake the churches, has cast into some people doubt about the Spirit, it is necessary to run back to the source of the faith from which the fathers at Nicaea drew when they made their statement of faith. What, then, is the perfection of our faith?
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius, writing on behalf of a synod, is answering the recipients' inquiry about the faith by affirming the Nicene creed and explaining why the fathers said nothing more extensive about the Holy Spirit.

title: The Lord's command as the rule of baptism, faith, and doxology
english: The Lord's tradition is what he commanded his holy disciples after his resurrection from the dead, when he ordered them: "Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19). Clearly we received the command not only to baptize in this way, but also to make disciples in this way. Through this command the sickness of Sabellius is shut out, because the three persons have been delivered to us clearly, and the mouths of the Anomoeans, the Arians, and the opponents of the Spirit are stopped, because the persons and hypostases are shown to be three, while the nature and the Godhead are confessed as one. It is necessary, then, for us to baptize as we were taught, to believe as we were baptized, and to glorify as we believed. For however much we examine with our minds and turn our thoughts in every direction, we can devise nothing between the creator and the creation. So if we separate the Spirit from the Godhead, it is necessary to number him with the creatures. And if we dare to call him a creature, how can he be joined in baptism? We denounce polytheism just as we denounce atheism. We proclaim neither three first principles nor three gods nor three different natures, but we know the Father as the first principle of all things, we reject none of the three persons, and we bring forward the majesty of the divine Scriptures and the testimonies concerning each one.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius is explaining that the Lord's baptismal command is the source of the faith, and he now quotes that command and draws out its anti-heretical force.

title: Closing exhortation to peace and right glorification of the Spirit
english: But since discussing these matters in fine detail would exceed the measure of a letter, and since we have trusted that your love will be satisfied with the main point of our exposition and will add the rest from your own resources—for, as the saying goes, give a wise man an opportunity and he will be wiser—we consider what we have written to be sufficient. To this it is enough to add a brief exhortation.

We urge you to remain sons of peace, so that you may fulfill the apostolic command, being of one soul, thinking the one thing, and sharing in the sufferings endured for Christ. Do not give the evil one a chance to separate what has been well joined together, and do not make yourselves easier prey for the wolves by division, thereby confirming their prayers. For we have learned how many struggles you have undergone for the sake of orthodoxy.

Since you have overcome the threats and the pressures from your adversaries, give no opportunity to division, lest hatred creeping in little by little, if it finds a place, may set great cliffs under you. But in your doxologies you must glorify the Spirit together with the Father and the Son, and know this: those who, through blasphemy against the Spirit, incur the unforgivable sin vainly reject communion with the Arians. For they will be condemned with them.

We pray that you, having kept the body of the church uncut and without quarreling, may pass the remaining time in this present age peacefully, and may stand gloriously before the judgment seat of Christ on the day of judgment.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius is closing his synodal letter, having just affirmed the Trinity and the Spirit's place in the Godhead.
